items.title: A client with heart failure has severe dyspnea, diffuse crackles, pink frothy sputum, and SpO₂ 82%.
items.content: answer:Position upright, support oxygenation/ventilation, and activate emergency response.
items.rationale: Pulmonary edema causes acute gas-exchange failure; respiratory support and escalation are immediate.

items.title: A client with AKI has potassium 6.8 mEq/L and peaked T waves.
items.content: answer:Continuous ECG, IV calcium as prescribed, potassium-shifting therapy, and definitive potassium removal.
items.rationale: Calcium stabilizes myocardium; insulin/dextrose and beta agonists shift potassium, while dialysis or other therapies remove it.

items.title: A client taking warfarin reports melena and dizziness.
items.content: answer:Assess hemodynamics, hold further dose pending urgent review, and obtain CBC/INR as ordered.
items.rationale: Melena suggests GI bleeding; assess shock and anticoagulation status.

items.title: Twenty minutes after birth, a client has heavy bleeding and a boggy fundus.
items.content: finding:Twenty minutes after birth, a client has heavy bleeding and a boggy fundus.|classification:Postpartum hemorrhage|key:Massage fundus, call for assistance, activate hemorrhage response, and prepare uterotonics/resuscitation.
items.rationale: Uterine atony is a common cause of postpartum hemorrhage.

items.title: A child has high fever, drooling, muffled voice, stridor, and tripod positioning.
items.content: finding:A child has high fever, drooling, muffled voice, stridor, and tripod positioning.|classification:Epiglottitis|key:Keep calm and upright; summon airway experts; do not inspect the throat.
items.rationale: Throat examination or agitation can precipitate complete airway obstruction.

items.title: A client develops facial droop and aphasia 35 minutes ago.
items.content: completion:Activate stroke response, document last-known-well, check glucose, and prepare urgent noncontrast CT.
items.rationale: Time, glucose, and imaging guide stroke treatment and exclude hemorrhage/mimics.

items.title: A client with pneumonia is confused, BP 82/46 mm Hg, and lactate 4.6 mmol/L.
items.content: condition:Sepsis|actions:Activate sepsis response, obtain cultures if no delay, give prompt antibiotics and prescribed crystalloid.|monitor:clinical status, relevant vital signs, and organ function
items.rationale: Hypotension, elevated lactate, and confusion indicate infection with hypoperfusion.

items.title: A client on magnesium sulfate has RR 9/min, absent reflexes, and urine output 18 mL/hr.
items.content: segments:A client on magnesium sulfate has RR 9/min, absent reflexes, and urine output 18 mL/hr.|correct:1
items.rationale: Respiratory depression, absent reflexes, and oliguria indicate magnesium accumulation.

items.title: A client is prescribed heparin 18 units/kg/hr and weighs 72 kg. The infusion contains 50 units/mL. Calculate the rate in mL/hr.
items.rationale: 18 × 72 = 1,296 units/hr; 1,296 ÷ 50 = 25.92 mL/hr, rounded to 25.9. Verify with the institutional high-alert medication process.

items.title: A client with DKA has glucose 580 mg/dL, pH 7.12, and potassium 2.9 mEq/L.
items.content: 1. Assess immediate safety/ABCs; 2. Escalate and obtain focused assessment; 3. Initiate prescribed intervention: Replace potassium and monitor ECG before starting insulin per protocol. 4. Reassess and document response.
items.rationale: Insulin shifts potassium intracellularly and can precipitate fatal dysrhythmia when potassium is severely low.

items.title: A client with tibial fracture has escalating pain, tense swelling, and pain with passive stretch; pulse remains palpable.
items.content: answer:Notify orthopedic surgeon immediately and prepare for urgent pressure-relief evaluation.
items.rationale: Pain out of proportion and passive-stretch pain are early signs; pulses may remain until late.

items.title: A client develops chills, flank pain, and fever 10 minutes after RBC transfusion begins.
items.content: initial:A client develops chills, flank pain, and fever 10 minutes after RBC transfusion begins.|interpretation:Stop transfusion immediately; maintain IV access with saline/new tubing and notify provider/blood bank.|rationale:The findings suggest acute hemolytic reaction.
items.rationale: The findings suggest acute hemolytic reaction.

items.title: Creatinine rises from 0.9 to 2.6 mg/dL and urine output falls to 10 mL/hr.
items.content: answer:Notify provider; assess volume status, potassium, fluid balance, and nephrotoxic exposures.
items.rationale: Rising creatinine with oliguria indicates worsening renal function.

items.title: A client with COPD is somnolent, RR 8/min, pH 7.25, and PaCO₂ 76 mm Hg.
items.content: answer:Escalate respiratory support and prepare for noninvasive or invasive ventilation.
items.rationale: Hypercapnic acidosis with somnolence indicates ventilatory failure.

items.title: During antibiotic infusion, a client develops wheezing, tongue swelling, and BP 76/40 mm Hg.
items.content: answer:Stop medication, give IM epinephrine per protocol, and activate emergency response.
items.rationale: Epinephrine is first-line for anaphylaxis; antihistamines are adjuncts.

items.title: A client with hematemesis is pale, HR 130/min, and BP 78/44 mm Hg.
items.content: answer:Activate emergency response, support ABCs, establish large-bore IV access, and prepare blood resuscitation.
items.rationale: The client has hemorrhagic shock; stabilize and prepare definitive hemostasis.

items.title: A client with cirrhosis is confused, has asterixis, and has been constipated.
items.content: finding:A client with cirrhosis is confused, has asterixis, and has been constipated.|classification:Hepatic encephalopathy|key:Administer prescribed lactulose and monitor mental status, stool frequency, hydration, and electrolytes.
items.rationale: Lactulose reduces ammonia absorption; constipation and bleeding can precipitate encephalopathy.

items.title: A client has severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and elevated lipase.
items.content: finding:A client has severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and elevated lipase.|classification:Acute pancreatitis|key:Provide prescribed IV fluids, analgesia, antiemetics, and oral/enteral nutrition as tolerated.
items.rationale: Supportive care treats pain and volume depletion; early nutrition is preferred when tolerated.

items.title: A client has fever, neck stiffness, photophobia, petechiae, and confusion.
items.content: completion:Initiate droplet precautions and urgent evaluation for bacterial meningitis/sepsis.
items.rationale: Meningococcal disease spreads by droplets and can progress rapidly.

items.title: A client who stopped chronic prednisone has vomiting, BP 78/42, hyponatremia, and hypoglycemia.
items.content: condition:Adrenal crisis|actions:Prepare IV hydrocortisone and isotonic fluids with dextrose as prescribed.|monitor:clinical status, relevant vital signs, and organ function
items.rationale: Adrenal crisis causes life-threatening hypotension and metabolic disturbance.

items.title: After cardiac surgery, a client develops hypotension, JVD, and muffled heart sounds.
items.content: segments:After cardiac surgery, a client develops hypotension, JVD, and muffled heart sounds.|correct:1
items.rationale: Beck triad indicates impaired ventricular filling and obstructive shock.

items.title: A client weighs 68 kg and is prescribed a crystalloid bolus of 30 mL/kg. Calculate the total volume in mL.
items.rationale: 68 × 30 = 2,040 mL. Administer according to the order and reassess perfusion and fluid tolerance.

items.title: After C5 injury, a client has BP 72/38, HR 42, and warm dry skin.
items.content: 1. Assess immediate safety/ABCs; 2. Escalate and obtain focused assessment; 3. Initiate prescribed intervention: Maintain spinal alignment and support circulation/respiration with prescribed therapy. 4. Reassess and document response.
items.rationale: Loss of sympathetic tone causes hypotension, bradycardia, and vasodilation.

items.title: A client with T4 injury develops pounding headache and BP 218/112 mm Hg.
items.content: answer:Sit upright, loosen clothing, and assess bladder drainage for obstruction.
items.rationale: Autonomic dysreflexia is a hypertensive emergency; remove triggers.

items.title: A septic client develops bilateral infiltrates, poor lung compliance, and severe hypoxemia despite oxygen.
items.content: initial:A septic client develops bilateral infiltrates, poor lung compliance, and severe hypoxemia despite oxygen.|interpretation:Escalate critical care and prepare lung-protective ventilation while treating sepsis.|rationale:ARDS causes noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and refractory hypoxemia.
items.rationale: ARDS causes noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and refractory hypoxemia.

items.title: An alert client has glucose 54 mg/dL and can swallow safely.
items.content: answer:Give 15 g rapid carbohydrate and recheck glucose in 15 minutes.
items.rationale: The 15-15 approach treats mild/moderate hypoglycemia in an alert client.

items.title: An unconscious client has glucose 32 mg/dL and cannot swallow.
items.content: answer:Give IV dextrose or glucagon per protocol and protect airway.
items.rationale: Oral carbohydrate creates aspiration risk in an unconscious client.

items.title: A client has unilateral calf warmth, swelling, and tenderness.
items.content: answer:Do not massage the leg; assess for PE symptoms and arrange diagnostic evaluation.
items.rationale: Massage is avoided with suspected DVT; dyspnea/chest pain may indicate PE.

items.title: A client has sudden severe leg pain, pallor, coolness, paresthesia, and absent pulse.
items.content: answer:Activate vascular emergency response and prepare for urgent revascularization.
items.rationale: Acute arterial occlusion threatens limb viability.

items.title: A fire victim has facial burns, soot in the mouth, and hoarseness.
items.content: finding:A fire victim has facial burns, soot in the mouth, and hoarseness.|classification:Burn inhalation injury|key:Prepare early controlled intubation and administer high-concentration oxygen.
items.rationale: Airway edema can progress rapidly after inhalation injury.

items.title: A fire victim has headache and confusion but SpO₂ reads 99%.
items.content: finding:A fire victim has headache and confusion but SpO₂ reads 99%.|classification:Carbon monoxide poisoning|key:Administer 100% oxygen and obtain co-oximetry evaluation.
items.rationale: Conventional pulse oximetry cannot distinguish carboxyhemoglobin reliably.

items.title: A client has frequent watery stools after clindamycin.
items.content: completion:Use contact precautions, soap-and-water hand hygiene, and sporicidal cleaning.
items.rationale: C. difficile spores resist alcohol hand rub.

items.title: A chemotherapy client has temperature 38.4°C and ANC 280/mm³.
items.content: condition:Neutropenic fever|actions:Notify provider urgently, obtain ordered cultures, and administer prompt empiric antibiotics.|monitor:clinical status, relevant vital signs, and organ function
items.rationale: Febrile neutropenia is an oncologic emergency.

items.title: A septic client has oozing IV sites, thrombocytopenia, prolonged PT/aPTT, and low fibrinogen.
items.content: segments:A septic client has oozing IV sites, thrombocytopenia, prolonged PT/aPTT, and low fibrinogen.|correct:1
items.rationale: DIC consumes platelets and clotting factors and causes bleeding/thrombosis.

items.title: A child weighs 18 kg and is prescribed 10 mg/kg per dose. The liquid contains 120 mg per 5 mL. Calculate the volume in mL.
items.rationale: Dose = 18 × 10 = 180 mg. Concentration = 24 mg/mL. Volume = 180 ÷ 24 = 7.5 mL.

items.title: A client with myasthenia has weak cough, dysphagia, and falling vital capacity.
items.content: 1. Assess immediate safety/ABCs; 2. Escalate and obtain focused assessment; 3. Initiate prescribed intervention: Activate critical-care/airway response, prepare ventilatory support, and keep NPO pending swallow assessment. 4. Reassess and document response.
items.rationale: Bulbar and respiratory weakness can progress to ventilatory failure.

items.title: A client with ascending weakness develops facial weakness and declining vital capacity.
items.content: answer:Perform serial respiratory mechanics and urgent airway/critical-care evaluation.
items.rationale: Guillain-Barré can progress to respiratory paralysis and autonomic instability.

items.title: A client has a hot swollen knee, fever, and inability to bear weight.
items.content: initial:A client has a hot swollen knee, fever, and inability to bear weight.|interpretation:Prepare urgent joint aspiration/culture, IV antibiotics, and possible drainage.|rationale:Septic arthritis can rapidly destroy cartilage.
items.rationale: Septic arthritis can rapidly destroy cartilage.

items.title: A client with diabetic foot ulcer has deep bone pain, fever, and draining sinus.
items.content: answer:Evaluate for osteomyelitis, obtain cultures, and prepare targeted antimicrobial treatment.
items.rationale: Bone infection may follow contiguous spread from a chronic ulcer.

items.title: A client has distention, bilious vomiting, and no flatus.
items.content: answer:Keep NPO, administer prescribed IV fluids, and prepare NG decompression.
items.rationale: Obstruction causes fluid sequestration and aspiration risk.

items.title: A client with atrial fibrillation has sudden severe abdominal pain out of proportion to exam and elevated lactate.
items.content: answer:Activate urgent vascular/surgical evaluation and prepare imaging/intervention.
items.rationale: Embolic bowel ischemia is time-critical.

items.title: A surgical incision opens and bowel is visible.
items.content: answer:Cover organs with sterile saline-moistened dressings, keep NPO, and summon immediate surgical assistance.
items.rationale: Do not reinsert organs; protect tissue and prepare for surgery.

items.title: A client has intact sacral skin with nonblanchable erythema.
items.content: finding:A client has intact sacral skin with nonblanchable erythema.|classification:Pressure injury|key:Classify as stage 1 pressure injury and offload pressure.
items.rationale: Stage 1 is intact skin with nonblanchable erythema.

items.title: A client 36 hours after femur fracture develops hypoxemia, confusion, and petechiae.
items.content: finding:A client 36 hours after femur fracture develops hypoxemia, confusion, and petechiae.|classification:Fat embolism syndrome|key:Provide respiratory support and urgent critical-care evaluation.
items.rationale: The classic triad includes respiratory distress, neurologic changes, and petechiae.

items.title: A client with sickle cell disease develops fever, chest pain, cough, and SpO₂ 88%.
items.content: completion:Escalate urgently, provide oxygen for hypoxemia, and prepare prescribed antibiotics/analgesia.
items.rationale: Acute chest syndrome is life-threatening.

items.title: After chemotherapy, a client has potassium 6.4, phosphate 7.0, uric acid 11, and rising creatinine.
items.content: condition:Tumor lysis syndrome|actions:Initiate telemetry, prescribed hydration/urate-lowering therapy, and urgent electrolyte management.|monitor:clinical status, relevant vital signs, and organ function
items.rationale: Cell lysis causes life-threatening electrolyte abnormalities and AKI.

items.title: A client with Graves disease has fever 40°C, HR 168/min, agitation, and diarrhea.
items.content: segments:A client with Graves disease has fever 40°C, HR 168/min, agitation, and diarrhea.|correct:1
items.rationale: Thyroid storm is a life-threatening hypermetabolic crisis.

items.title: A client is prescribed 1.2 g of an antibiotic. The reconstituted concentration is 400 mg/mL. Calculate the volume in mL.
A client has sudden severe eye pain, halos, blurred vision, and nausea.
items.content: 1. Assess immediate safety/ABCs; 2. Escalate and obtain focused assessment; 3. Initiate prescribed intervention: Arrange immediate ophthalmic treatment for acute angle-closure glaucoma. 4. Reassess and document response.
items.rationale: Elevated intraocular pressure can rapidly cause permanent vision loss.

items.title: A client with abdominal pain has rigid abdomen, rebound tenderness, fever, and tachycardia.
items.content: answer:Escalate for urgent surgical evaluation and prescribed antibiotics/resuscitation.
items.rationale: Peritoneal signs with systemic symptoms indicate an urgent abdominal process.

items.title: A client with neck trauma develops stridor, inability to speak, and expanding swelling.
items.content: initial:A client with neck trauma develops stridor, inability to speak, and expanding swelling.|interpretation:Activate emergency airway response and prepare definitive airway management.|rationale:Stridor and expanding neck hematoma indicate impending obstruction.
items.rationale: Stridor and expanding neck hematoma indicate impending obstruction.

items.title: After chest trauma, a client has absent breath sounds, dullness, hypotension, and tachycardia.
items.content: answer:Activate trauma response and prepare chest tube and blood resuscitation.
items.rationale: Pleural blood impairs ventilation and causes volume loss.

items.title: A client develops sudden dyspnea, hypotension, absent unilateral breath sounds, and tracheal deviation.
items.content: answer:Prepare for immediate decompression by a qualified clinician.
items.rationale: Tension pneumothorax causes obstructive shock.

items.title: A client has sharp chest pain relieved by leaning forward and a friction rub.
items.content: answer:Assess for effusion/tamponade and administer prescribed anti-inflammatory therapy.
items.rationale: Positional pleuritic pain and friction rub are characteristic.

items.title: A client with severe aortic stenosis develops syncope and chest pain during ambulation.
items.content: answer:Stop activity, assess hemodynamics, and escalate urgently.
items.rationale: Fixed outflow obstruction can cause syncope and ischemia.

items.title: A client taking digoxin reports nausea and yellow-green halos; apical pulse is 48/min.
items.content: finding:A client taking digoxin reports nausea and yellow-green halos; apical pulse is 48/min.|classification:Digoxin toxicity|key:Withhold digoxin and notify prescriber; obtain level and electrolytes as ordered.
items.rationale: Bradycardia, GI symptoms, and visual changes suggest toxicity.

items.title: A client taking lithium has coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, and confusion after diarrhea.
items.content: finding:A client taking lithium has coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, and confusion after diarrhea.|classification:Lithium toxicity|key:Hold lithium and obtain urgent serum level and renal/electrolyte assessment.
items.rationale: Dehydration reduces lithium clearance and may cause toxicity.

items.title: A client taking serotonergic drugs develops fever, agitation, clonus, and hyperreflexia.
items.content: completion:Stop serotonergic agents and initiate urgent supportive care.
items.rationale: Clonus and hyperreflexia with autonomic instability are characteristic.

items.title: A client taking haloperidol develops high fever, lead-pipe rigidity, confusion, and elevated CK.
items.content: condition:Neuroleptic malignant syndrome|actions:Stop antipsychotic and initiate emergency supportive care.|monitor:clinical status, relevant vital signs, and organ function
items.rationale: NMS causes rigidity, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, and autonomic instability.

items.title: A client with chronic alcohol use has confusion, ataxia, and abnormal eye movements.
items.content: segments:A client with chronic alcohol use has confusion, ataxia, and abnormal eye movements.|correct:1
items.rationale: The triad suggests thiamine deficiency; early treatment prevents progression.

items.title: A client weighs 70 kg and is prescribed factor VIII 40 units/kg. Calculate the dose in units.
items.content: 2800|units|0
items.rationale: 70 × 40 = 2,800 units. Verify product-specific dosing with the hematology plan.

items.title: A client with acute hepatitis becomes confused, INR 3.2, and glucose 54 mg/dL.
items.content: 1. Assess immediate safety/ABCs; 2. Escalate and obtain focused assessment; 3. Initiate prescribed intervention: Escalate for critical-care/transplant evaluation, monitor airway/neurologic status, and treat hypoglycemia. 4. Reassess and document response.
items.rationale: Encephalopathy and coagulopathy indicate severe hepatic dysfunction.

items.title: A client with cirrhosis has large-volume hematemesis and hypotension.
items.content: answer:Protect airway, establish large-bore IV access, resuscitate, and prepare vasoactive therapy/endoscopy.
items.rationale: Variceal bleeding can cause rapid exsanguination and aspiration.

items.title: A client with gallstones has RUQ pain, fever, jaundice, hypotension, and confusion.
items.content: initial:A client with gallstones has RUQ pain, fever, jaundice, hypotension, and confusion.|interpretation:Activate urgent sepsis care, administer antibiotics, and prepare biliary drainage.|rationale:Severe ascending cholangitis requires antibiotics and source control.
items.rationale: Severe ascending cholangitis requires antibiotics and source control.

items.title: A client with ureteral stone has fever, rigors, hydronephrosis, and hypotension.
items.content: answer:Urgent antibiotics and decompression of the obstructed urinary system.
items.rationale: Infected obstruction is a urologic emergency.

items.title: A postoperative client has suprapubic discomfort and bladder scan 780 mL.
items.content: answer:Perform prescribed bladder decompression and monitor urine output.
items.rationale: Significant retention requires management and monitoring.

items.title: A client has jaundice, dark urine, falling hemoglobin, and elevated indirect bilirubin.
items.content: answer:Evaluate for hemolysis and monitor renal/hemodynamic status.
items.rationale: Hemolysis releases hemoglobin and increases indirect bilirubin.

items.title: A client has fatigue, microcytosis, and low ferritin.
items.content: answer:Evaluate iron deficiency and source of blood loss; reinforce prescribed replacement.
items.rationale: Low ferritin and microcytosis are typical of iron deficiency.

items.title: A client has macrocytosis, paresthesia, and impaired vibration sense.
items.content: finding:A client has macrocytosis, paresthesia, and impaired vibration sense.|classification:Vitamin B12 deficiency|key:Evaluate B12 deficiency and prepare replacement therapy.
items.rationale: B12 deficiency causes macrocytic anemia and neurologic injury.

items.title: A client has pancytopenia, fatigue, infections, and bruising.
items.content: finding:A client has pancytopenia, fatigue, infections, and bruising.|classification:Aplastic anemia|key:Institute infection and bleeding precautions and arrange urgent hematology evaluation.
items.rationale: Pancytopenia increases infection, anemia, and bleeding risks.

items.title: A dialysis client misses treatment and develops severe dyspnea, crackles, hypertension, and SpO₂ 80%.
items.content: completion:Support oxygenation/ventilation and arrange urgent dialysis/ultrafiltration.
items.rationale: Fluid overload causing pulmonary edema is life-threatening.

items.title: A client with malignancy has calcium 14.2 mg/dL, confusion, constipation, and dehydration.
items.content: condition:Severe hypercalcemia|actions:Initiate prescribed isotonic hydration and calcium-lowering therapy with ECG/renal monitoring.|monitor:clinical status, relevant vital signs, and organ function
items.rationale: Severe hypercalcemia causes neurologic, renal, and cardiac complications.

items.title: A client has sodium 112 mEq/L and a seizure.
items.content: segments:A client has sodium 112 mEq/L and a seizure.|correct:1
items.rationale: Severe symptomatic hyponatremia is a neurologic emergency.

items.title: A client receives 1,000 mL of IV fluid over 8 hours. Calculate the pump rate in mL/hr.
items.rationale: 1,000 ÷ 8 = 125 mL/hr. Confirm the prescribed fluid and patient-specific restrictions.

items.title: A client has sodium 168 mEq/L, intense thirst, restlessness, and confusion.
items.content: 1. Assess immediate safety/ABCs; 2. Escalate and obtain focused assessment; 3. Initiate prescribed intervention: Correct free-water deficit gradually with frequent sodium and neurologic monitoring. 4. Reassess and document response.
items.rationale: Hypernatremia causes cellular dehydration; overly rapid correction risks cerebral edema.

items.title: A client with DKA has pH 7.20, bicarbonate 10 mEq/L, and Kussmaul respirations.
items.content: answer:Identify high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and treat DKA per protocol.
items.rationale: Ketone accumulation lowers bicarbonate and pH.

items.title: A client hyperventilating during panic has pH 7.50 and PaCO₂ 28 mm Hg.
items.content: initial:A client hyperventilating during panic has pH 7.50 and PaCO₂ 28 mm Hg.|interpretation:Identify respiratory alkalosis and assess/treat the cause of hyperventilation.|rationale:Excess ventilation lowers PaCO₂ and raises pH.
items.rationale: Excess ventilation lowers PaCO₂ and raises pH.

items.title: A client with prolonged vomiting has pH 7.49 and bicarbonate 34 mEq/L.
items.content: answer:Identify metabolic alkalosis and assess volume/chloride and potassium deficits.
items.rationale: Loss of gastric acid raises bicarbonate relative to acid.

items.title: A client with opioid toxicity has pH 7.24 and PaCO₂ 68 mm Hg.
items.content: answer:Identify respiratory acidosis and support ventilation.
items.rationale: CO₂ retention lowers pH.

items.title: A client taking warfarin has sudden severe headache, vomiting, and confusion; INR is 5.6.
items.content: answer:Arrange emergency brain imaging and prescribed warfarin reversal.
items.rationale: Anticoagulant-associated intracranial hemorrhage requires rapid reversal.

items.title: A client reports worst headache of life with neck stiffness and vomiting.
items.content: answer:Activate emergency neurologic evaluation and obtain urgent noncontrast CT.
items.rationale: Thunderclap headache with meningismus is classic for SAH.

items.title: Six days after aneurysmal SAH, a client develops new unilateral weakness.
items.content: finding:Six days after aneurysmal SAH, a client develops new unilateral weakness.|classification:Cerebral vasospasm|key:Notify neurocritical team immediately and evaluate for delayed cerebral ischemia/vasospasm.
items.rationale: New focal deficit days after SAH may indicate vasospasm.

items.title: A client with TBI develops declining consciousness, vomiting, and unequal pupils.
items.content: finding:A client with TBI develops declining consciousness, vomiting, and unequal pupils.|classification:Increased intracranial pressure|key:Activate emergency neurocritical response, protect airway, and prepare urgent imaging/ICP management.
items.rationale: These are signs of rising ICP and possible herniation.

items.title: A client develops sudden diplopia, vertigo, ataxia, and dysarthria.
items.content: completion:Activate stroke response and document last-known-well.
items.rationale: Brainstem/cerebellar ischemia causes ocular, balance, speech, and swallowing deficits.

items.title: A client with stroke coughs and has a wet voice after water.
items.content: condition:Stroke dysphagia|actions:Stop oral intake, maintain NPO, and arrange validated swallow assessment.|monitor:clinical status, relevant vital signs, and organ function
items.rationale: Coughing and wet voice suggest aspiration risk.

items.title: A client with right hemisphere stroke ignores food on the left and attempts unsafe transfers.
items.content: segments:A client with right hemisphere stroke ignores food on the left and attempts unsafe transfers.|correct:1
items.rationale: Neglect and impulsivity increase injury risk.

items.title: A client has BP 86/50 mm Hg. Calculate MAP using (SBP + 2 × DBP) ÷ 3. Round to the nearest whole number.
items.content: 62|mm Hg|0

items.title: A client reports a specific plan and intent to die tonight.
items.content: 1. Assess immediate safety/ABCs; 2. Escalate and obtain focused assessment; 3. Initiate prescribed intervention: Maintain continuous observation, remove access to means, and initiate emergency safety evaluation. 4. Reassess and document response.
items.rationale: A specific plan and imminent timeframe indicate high acute risk.

items.title: A client reports voices commanding self-harm.
items.content: answer:Ask directly whether the client intends to act and has a plan or access to means.
items.rationale: Command hallucinations require direct safety assessment.

items.title: A client has decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, grandiosity, and risky spending.
items.content: initial:A client has decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, grandiosity, and risky spending.|interpretation:Maintain safety, reduce stimulation, and administer prescribed treatment.|rationale:These are characteristic manic symptoms.
items.rationale: These are characteristic manic symptoms.

items.title: A client taking clozapine reports fever and sore throat.
items.content: answer:Arrange urgent CBC/ANC assessment and prescriber notification.
items.rationale: Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia/agranulocytosis.

items.title: A client is unresponsive, RR 5/min, and has pinpoint pupils.
items.content: answer:Support ventilation, activate emergency response, and administer naloxone per protocol.
items.rationale: Respiratory depression is life-threatening; naloxone may need repeating.

items.title: A client overdoses on propranolol and develops HR 38/min and hypotension.
items.content: answer:Activate toxicology response and prepare prescribed glucagon/hemodynamic support.
items.rationale: Beta blocker toxicity causes bradycardia, hypotension, and possible hypoglycemia.

items.title: A client receives twice the prescribed beta-blocker dose and is symptomatic.
items.content: answer:Assess ABCs and hemodynamic status and activate urgent clinical response.
items.rationale: Treat immediate instability before reporting/documenting the error.

items.title: A client develops flushing and pruritus during rapid vancomycin infusion.
items.content: finding:A client develops flushing and pruritus during rapid vancomycin infusion.|classification:Vancomycin infusion reaction|key:Pause/slow infusion per protocol, assess for hypotension/airway symptoms, and notify provider.
items.rationale: Rate-related infusion reaction may improve with slower administration.

items.title: A client receiving gentamicin reports tinnitus and has rising creatinine.
items.content: finding:A client receiving gentamicin reports tinnitus and has rising creatinine.|classification:Aminoglycoside toxicity|key:Notify prescriber and assess for ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity; review levels and renal function.
items.rationale: Aminoglycosides can injure hearing and kidneys.

items.title: A client receiving contrast develops stridor, wheezing, tongue swelling, and hypotension.
items.content: completion:Stop contrast and administer IM epinephrine while activating emergency response.
items.rationale: Severe contrast reaction with airway/circulatory compromise is anaphylaxis.

items.title: A client on postoperative day 2 has distention, nausea, absent bowel sounds, and no flatus.
items.content: condition:Postoperative ileus|actions:Assess for complications and follow orders for NPO/decompression.|monitor:clinical status, relevant vital signs, and organ function
items.rationale: Delayed bowel motility causes distention and nausea.

items.title: A client with ileostomy has watery output, dizziness, and low urine output.
items.content: segments:A client with ileostomy has watery output, dizziness, and low urine output.|correct:1
items.rationale: High output can cause dehydration and AKI.

items.title: A client has a serum sodium of 140 mEq/L, chloride 104 mEq/L, and bicarbonate 16 mEq/L. Calculate the anion gap using Na − (Cl + HCO₃).
items.content: 20|mEq/L|0
